newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish central banker favours bourse, OM merger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish central banker favours bourse, OM merger.

text.p: Stefan Ingves, deputy governor of the Swedish Riksbank central bank, said on Monday he was positive to a merger between the Stockholm Stock Exchange and derivatives and futures trader OM.
"An integration of the whole transaction chain would simplify the access to the Swedish market and thereby strengthen its competitiveness," Ingves said in a report.
The report deals with how the infrastructure of the Swedish financial market can be effective in the future.
A well functioning financial market is an important part of the economy, he said.
"Considering this as well as the increasing international competition, measures should be taken quickly to retain and develop the Swedish market," he said in a statement.
Ingves emphasized the importance of the possible merger gaining general acceptance.
He did not think the state's share in the securities transaction registrar VPC should be part of the ongoing discussions about OM and the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
The state owns parts of both the Swedish Stock Exchange and VPC.
Ingves said a special negotiator should be appointed to safeguard the interest of the state in the discussions on the financial infrastructure.
He added that current limitations regarding accepting new stock exchange members should be removed and direct trade should be easier to undertake.

The changes taking place in the financial sector make heavy demands on the Financial Inspectorate which should be given resources, Ingves said. These resources should be financed by the financial sector.
